profile.reading:
Per NTT's own Global Data Centers facility page, this building, NTT VA11, is located at 7251 Grove Hill Blvd, Gainesville, VA 20155, geographically distinct from NTT's core Ashburn campus (VA1-VA9) despite sharing the "VA" numbering; Gainesville sits roughly 20 miles southwest of Ashburn in Prince William County, part of the broader Northern Virginia data center corridor pushing outward from the original Loudoun County core. The operator publishes over 300,000 square feet of IT space and 96 megawatts of critical IT load, delivered as N+1 distributed redundancy across 8-megawatt vaults; VA11 was not yet operational as of this registry's research, with NTT's own page stating an opening in early 2027 and the facility currently in pre-lease.

Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to new Northern Virginia capacity like VA11. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates that will raise a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers effective January 1, 2027; data center customers with 25 megawatts or more of demand, a threshold VA11's planned 96 megawatts far exceeds, must sign 14-year mandatory contracts and pay a minimum 85% of transmission and distribution costs and a minimum 60% of generation costs regardless of actual usage, per Inside Climate News's reporting on the SCC decision. Prince William County has separately debated its own data center zoning and siting rules as Northern Virginia's buildout pushes into new jurisdictions beyond Loudoun County.

NTT's US Global Data Centers footprint spans seven named campuses in total: Ashburn, Virginia at 224 megawatts; Chicago, Illinois at more than 200 megawatts; Dallas, Texas at 160 megawatts; Hillsboro, Oregon at 126 megawatts; Phoenix, Arizona at 240 megawatts; and a combined Sacramento/Santa Clara, California figure of 68 megawatts, totaling roughly 1,118 megawatts or more of disclosed US capacity, per the operator's own locations page. The US business operates under the NTT DATA Global Data Centers Americas name, the successor brand to RagingWire Data Centers, now under Japan's NTT DATA Group and parent Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation, a Tokyo Stock Exchange-listed company not subject to SEC 10-K filing requirements.

reading.body:
VA11 is a 96-megawatt facility in Gainesville, roughly 20 miles southwest of Northern Virginia's original Ashburn data center cluster, and is scheduled to open in early 2027. At typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, the published IT load translates to approximately 2,400 racks, though the operator specifies IT capacity delivered across 8-megawatt vaults with N+1 redundancy rather than as discrete rack counts. The facility is not yet operational and remains in pre-lease.

Virginia's regulatory environment has shifted materially in favor of large data center operations. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates that create a GS-5 tariff class for customers exceeding 25 megawatts, requiring 14-year contracts and mandating payment of at least 85 percent of transmission and distribution costs plus at least 60 percent of generation costs regardless of utilization. VA11's 96-megawatt planned draw places it well above that threshold and thus subject to these terms effective January 2027. Prince William County, where the facility sits, has separately begun deliberating data center zoning rules as the Northern Virginia buildout expands beyond Loudoun County's historic core.

Within Virginia's published data center capacity of 1,375.4 megawatts across 23 facilities, VA11 ranks third by size once it opens. NTT operates approximately 1,118 megawatts or more of disclosed US capacity across seven campuses, with Ashburn accounting for 224 megawatts. The registry has mapped 326 data center facilities in Virginia overall, though only 23 publish IT load figures.
